title: An-Nazi'at 79:1-8 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Written for quran/y7 lesson 21 (Pupil PDF worksheet: An-Nazi'at 79:1-8 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 21. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: وَٱلنَّٰزِعَٰتِ غَرْقًۭا (١) وَٱلنَّٰشِطَٰتِ نَشْطًۭا (٢) وَٱلسَّٰبِحَٰتِ سَبْحًۭا (٣) فَٱلسَّٰبِقَٰتِ سَبْقًۭا (٤) فَٱلْمُدَبِّرَٰتِ أَمْرًۭا (٥) يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ ٱلرَّاجِفَةُ (٦) تَتْبَعُهَا ٱلرَّادِفَةُ (٧) قُلُوبٌۭ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ وَاجِفَةٌ (٨)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: By those [angels] who extract with violence
And [by] those who remove with ease
And [by] those who glide [as if] swimming
And those who race each other in a race
On the Day the blast [of the Horn] will convulse [creation],
There will follow it the subsequent [one].

head: Word
Where
Rule
How to read it
rows: Tanween at a stop: becomes alif (madd 'iwad)
Sun letter ر; ة at a stop
Idgham with ghunnah: tanween into ي

questions.q: Chunk and link An-Nazi'at 79:1-8 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 79:1-8 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 79:1-8 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Find every tanween fathah in 79:1 to 5 and say how it is read at a stop.
questions.a: غَرْقًۭا، نَشْطًۭا، سَبْحًۭا، سَبْقًۭا، أَمْرًا: each becomes an alif (madd 'iwad, 2 counts).

questions.q: Why does the surah start with oaths before speaking of the Day?
questions.a: An oath shows how serious and certain the coming Day is.

questions.q: What will happen to hearts that Day (79:8)?
questions.a: A) They will tremble. 79:8: 'Hearts, that Day, will tremble.'

questions.q: An-Nazi'at 79:6: «يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: An-Nazi'at begins with oaths about angels doing their work. What does it tell you that Allah has angels for every task?
questions.a: Allah is in control of everything; nothing happens without His command, including the end of each life.
